🍺 Beijing has a bar where your drink comes with free DeepSeek tokens

Forget happy hour. In Beijing, you can now grab a drink and get free AI compute on the side.

AGI Bar, an AI-themed hangout in Zhongguancun, charges just 9.9 yuan ($1.50) for its signature drink and customers get unlimited DeepSeek tokens for coding through the bar’s AI agent.

The tokens run on two Nvidia DGX Spark machines sitting inside the bar. 

The place has become a meeting spot for AI developers, investors and students, hosting developer seminars, open-source AI events and parties for Chinese AI labs.

And the owner is taking the concept even further: much of the bar’s operations are already automated with AI, and humanoid robot waiters are reportedly on the way.

There’s just one problem… The bar is losing money because it gives away far more drinks and AI tokens than it sells.

🤖 Claude just designed 354 protein binders that worked in the lab

Anthropic gave its AI agents 16 biological targets and asked them to design entirely new protein minibinders. Claude generated 1,320 designs, and 354 were experimentally confirmed to work.

Across 15 targets that were tested, Claude produced successful binders for 14, with hit rates between 22.6% and 35.1%, roughly 2–3× higher than the 10–15% rates Anthropic says are typical for current de novo protein-design campaigns.

Claude wasn’t simply generating protein sequences. It autonomously coordinated specialized protein-design, sequence-design and protein-folding models, optimized candidates, filtered them computationally and decided which designs were worth sending to the lab.

Then Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience physically produced the proteins and tested them.

Against RBX1, Claude achieved a 40% hit rate. A previous protein-design competition managed just 3.7%.
